//: The dependency inventory. Every third-party file this site serves, with the
version it is, the hash it should have, and the date somebody last checked it
against the advisories. tools/depscan.py reads this.
A vendored file has one advantage over a CDN - nobody else can change it - and
one disadvantage - nobody else will patch it either. This file is what turns the
disadvantage back into a task with a date on it.
sha256 is not decoration: it is checked on every run, so a modified library in
the working tree, in a deploy, or in a pull request shows up as a failure rather

libraries.name: firebase-js-sdk (app-compat)
libraries.note: Behind by two majors. Nothing in the app uses an API that changed, so the upgrade is a swap of seven files and a re-run of tools/mergetest.js and tools/authtest.js.

libraries.name: firebase-js-sdk (analytics-compat)
libraries.note: Loaded only if a visitor accepts measurement in the consent banner. Not referenced from index.html.

libraries.name: three.js
libraries.note: Well behind. It draws one WebGL gallery on the lookbook page and touches no user input, so the exposure is small - but 608KB of unmaintained WebGL is the largest single thing this site serves, and the honest fix is to drop it for a CSS gallery rather than to upgrade it.
